scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that the past is not a perfect guide, then argues it clearly helps us decide today; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose at about 400 words on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: Many of today's hardest choices closely resemble problems that people faced long ago.
Some people argue that knowing about the past cannot help us make important decisions today.
I strongly disagree, because the past offers lessons that guide wise decisions, even if it is not a perfect guide.

sections.role: Body 1 — Why the past has real limits

sentences.text: First, it is fair to admit that the past cannot answer every question we face today.
The world changes, and old solutions do not always fit new and unfamiliar problems.
For example, ancient ways of running a small village cannot simply be copied to govern a huge modern city.
This shows that we cannot blindly apply the past to the present without careful thought.
Relying too heavily on old examples can even blind us to what is genuinely new.
Each age does face some challenges that earlier generations never imagined.
To this extent, the past has real limits as a guide.

sections.role: Body 2 — Why the past clearly helps

sentences.text: Second, however, it is plainly false that the past cannot help us decide today.
History is full of lessons about which choices succeed and which ones end in disaster.
Consider how the study of past economic crashes helps leaders avoid repeating the same mistakes.
Such lessons show that knowing the past can directly improve the decisions we make now.
Even in personal life, remembering past mistakes helps us choose more wisely the next time.
Ignoring history would force every generation to relearn painful lessons from the very beginning.
The past, then, is one of the most useful guides we have for the present.
In conclusion, the past is not a perfect guide and cannot answer every modern question.
But knowing history clearly helps us make wiser decisions and avoid repeating old mistakes.
We decide best today when we learn from the past without being chained to it.
